verifications.claim: NASA is targeting the Artemis II mission for launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Next launch is Artemis II from Kennedy Space Center on Wednesday, April 1, 2026" "Launch: 6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 2026"
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly states the exact launch date and time for Artemis II as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "send four astronauts further in space than any humans before them... on a 10-day journey around the moon and back"; R2: "will set off to orbit the Moon"; R3: "send a crew of four astronauts on a trailblazing nine-day trip around the moon and back."
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references explicitly describe sending four astronauts around the Moon and back.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day flight test.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "10-day flight"; R2: "10-day mission"; R4: "10-day journey to the moon and back."
verifications.reasoning: Primary references consistently describe it as a 10-day mission/test flight; minor variation in R3 ('nine-day') does not contradict overall support.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first human moon mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "For the first time since 1972"; R3: "first crew to head for the moon since the Apollo 17 flight... more than 50 years ago."
verifications.reasoning: References directly confirm it as the first crewed lunar mission since 1972 (over 50 years).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is set to lift off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "from Kennedy Space Center in Florida"; R2: "at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida."
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of launch site as Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: The next launch date for Artemis II is as early as Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "As of Tuesday, March 31... Next launch is Artemis II... on Wednesday, April 1, 2026."
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly states the next launch as Wednesday, April 1, 2026, from a March 31 perspective.

verifications.claim: The vehicle for Artemis II is the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket carrying the Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "NASA's massive Space Launch System spacecraft"; R2: "Launching aboard the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket... Orion spacecraft"; R3: "NASA's Space Launch System rocket... Orion deep space crew capsule."
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm SLS rocket with Orion spacecraft for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: The purpose of Artemis II is to test deep-space capabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "verify modern human capabilities in deep space"; cited snippet: "This mission will test deep-space travel."
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states testing deep-space human capabilities.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is preparing for future long-term human exploration of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "pave the way for future crewed lunar exploration missions"; R2: "pave the way for long-term exploration and science on the lunar surface."
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly link Artemis II to paving way for long-term lunar exploration.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, as well as Jeremy Hansen from the Canadian Space Agency"; R3: "commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, astronaut Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen."
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names and affiliations match across references.

verifications.claim: Launch viewing for Artemis II is available from the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 from Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex site; R6: "Watching a live rocket launch... At Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex"; cited snippet: "Artemis II - Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex."
verifications.reasoning: R6 describes launch viewing from Visitor Complex; R2 is Artemis II page from same site, implying availability.
